text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:
- CDU and FDP pledge allegiance to the Bonn coalition government and vow that it will hold together. FDP chairman Wolfgang Gerhardt demands clarity about solidarity tax cut this week.
- More than 100,000 metal industry workers demonstrate in Bavaria against sick pay cuts
- Turkish President Demirel, on visit to Germany, says Turkey shares the values of Europe
- Reform communist PDS party, at strategy conference in Berlin, sets its sights on forming coalition with SPD and Greens
- Coalition searches for new concept on taxes in hopes of ending the prolonged dispute over the 1996 budget in one fell swoop.
- German rail will sell property with 13 billion marks over the next 15 years. Proceeds will be used in part to pay back old debts.
- Time has come for new initiatives to stimulate exports from eastern Germany. The region's manufacturers account for only 2 percent of Germany's exports.
- Chancellor Kohl calls on FDP to return to coalition discipline. FDP insists on sinking the solidarity tax by two percentage points in 1998.
- SPD leader Lafontaine says law allowing employers to cut sick pay should be scrapped.
- IG Metall says it will strike if necessary to maintain full sick pay benefits.
- Kohl warns the FDP against trying to raise their profile at expense of coalition
- Former German President Richard von Weizsaecker says Kohl will sign the German-Czech treaty this year.
- Germany is world's third largest book market, with book sales of $9.9 billion
